welcome.title: Welcome to {{app}}
welcome.content:
{{app}} keeps your notes, your snippets and your lists within reach of a shortcut.

- Cards file themselves: pinned, today, this week, older.
- The square chip on a card says which folder it lives in. Try the "Board" view at the top: folders are regions there, and notes are dropped into them with the mouse.
- Everything is local: the database lives in your user folder, nothing goes over the network.

These four notes are samples. Edit them, or send them to the trash: the "About → Getting started" menu tells the same story and does not go away.

settings.title: Preferences

behavior.title: Behavior
behavior.trayNote: Without a system tray the window minimizes and closes as usual: {{app}} refuses to hide where nothing could call it back.

security.title: Security
security.note: It opens the library at every launch. Changing it re-encrypts nothing: your notes stay sealed with the same key, which is why it takes a second rather than a rewrite.
security.dialogLead: The new one applies at the next launch. This session carries on as it is.
security.changed: Passphrase changed. The old one no longer opens the library, nor the copies kept beside it.
security.backupsNote: At most one copy a day, the last three kept beside the library — enough for an emptied trash or an update gone wrong. Not a defence against a dead disk: export somewhere else for that.
security.changedOneLeft: Passphrase changed, but one copy could not be rewrapped: it still opens with the old phrase.
security.changedSomeLeft: Passphrase changed, but {{count}} copies could not be rewrapped: they still open with the old phrase.
security.copiesNote: The copies kept beside the library are rewrapped with it. A key file you copied somewhere else will still open with the old phrase.
security.backupsLimit: A copy carries the notes and the key that opens them, not the attached files.

shortcuts.globalNote: These three work everywhere, window closed included, so each needs at least one modifier — without one the key would be swallowed in every application you use. A shortcut another application already holds is reported at startup.
shortcuts.canvasNote: These only act on the canvas, never while typing, so a bare letter is enough. Click the field, then press the combination.
shortcuts.fixedNote: The arrows, Escape, Tab and the Ctrl or Shift clicks do not move: they are the navigation, the way out and the selection, and a library you cannot step back through would be worse than a badly placed key.
shortcuts.needsModifier: A global shortcut needs at least Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Super.
shortcuts.reserved: That key is reserved for navigation.
shortcuts.conflict: {{accelerator}} answers several actions: {{actions}}. Only one will act.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.subtitle: What {{app}} can do, in the order you meet it.

notes.title: Notes and snippets
notes.body: A note carries a title, a body coloured by its language, a source and tags. Click a card to open it — or copy it without opening, from its own button.

spaces.title: Spaces to file things in
spaces.body: Every note lives in a space: “Personal”, “Work”, whatever you like. Deleting one always asks where its notes should go — they never leave with it.

folders.title: Folders, and a board
folders.body: A folder cuts a space into named, coloured regions, and the “Board” view shows them as such: drag a card in to file it, drop it on the background to take it out. Without a mouse: {{check}} to tick, then “File into”.

organise.title: Finding things: search, tags, filters
organise.body: Search runs through titles, bodies, sources and list items, accents included. The quick filters isolate the pinned ones or the ones carrying a deadline; tags and formats sit behind the button beside them.

fields.title: Fields to fill in
fields.body: Write a field in double braces inside a snippet and its value will be asked for at the moment you copy. What you type stays with the note, and a global variable proposes one for the whole library.

checklists.title: Lists to tick
checklists.body: A note is either a snippet or a todo list — and a list is ticked from the card, without opening it. In the editor, Enter adds an item and Alt with an arrow moves it.

palette.title: Pasting without leaving what you are doing
palette.body: {{palette}} opens the paste palette over any application: type, choose, it is on the clipboard. {{capture}} does the reverse and {{newNote}} opens an empty note, closed window included.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.body: Drop a file on the window while a note is open, or paste an image: it is copied beside the database and attached to the note. The card shows the count, and the preview grows on a click.

trash.title: A trash, and Ctrl+Z
trash.body: A deleted note goes to the trash and stays there for thirty days. The banner that follows offers to undo, and Ctrl+Z still does it once the banner is gone.

transfer.title: In and out
transfer.body: The File menu exports everything, one space or the selection to a file it can read back, and re-imports it without ever making a duplicate. “Copy as Markdown” puts the selection on the clipboard.

whatsNew.title: What's new
whatsNew.subtitle: The changelog shipped with the application. Deliberately untranslated.

vault.createLead: Choose a passphrase. {{app}} will ask for it once at every launch.
vault.noRecovery: ⚠️ This passphrase cannot be recovered. Lose it and the library goes with it — a plaintext export is the only copy that does not depend on it.
vault.unlockLead: Enter your passphrase to open your notes.
vault.damagedLead: SQLite refuses to read {{app}}'s database. A passphrase will not help — the file itself is broken, and writing to it now would make it worse.
vault.damagedAction: Set it aside and start fresh
vault.damagedNote: ⚠️ The damaged database and its attachments are moved into a folder of their own, and what can still be read is rescued beside them. Your passphrase does not change. {{app}} then opens on an empty library.
vault.setAside: Library set aside in {{path}}. Enter your passphrase to start on a fresh one.
vault.forgottenLead: There is no recovery: the phrase wraps the key that seals the notes, and nothing else opens it. What {{app}} can do is archive the library as it stands and open a fresh one for you.
vault.forgottenNote: Your notes are not recovered: they leave sealed and unreadable, in a dated folder beside the library. The key file goes with them — if the phrase comes back to you one day, the copy will still be there. The new library starts empty, with a phrase of your choosing.
vault.archived: Library archived, sealed, in {{path}}. Choose a phrase for the new one.

backups.none: No copy yet. The first one is taken at the next launch.
backups.confirm: Replace the whole library with the copy from {{when}}. Everything written since leaves the library — nothing is deleted, the current one is set aside in "replaced". You will have to type the passphrase again.
backups.restored: Library restored. The previous one is in {{path}}.

libraries.title: Libraries
libraries.lead: Each library has its own database, attachments, backups and passphrase. Nothing crosses from one to another.
